title: CLAUDE.md
text: package organized around three R6 classes plus family helper functions. Understanding three objects fastest way orient:

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Base R6 class representing one LANDIS-II extension’s configuration input files. supported extension subclass living R/ext_*.R file (e.g. R/ext_biomass_succession.R, R/ext_dynamic_fire.R, R/ext_original_fire.R, R/ext_social_climate_fire.R, R/ext_forc-succession.R, output extensions ext_output_*.R). subclass follows consistent pattern: 1. initialize() stashes parameters private fields, sets self$path, self$type (one "succession", "disturbance", "" — see .extTypes), primary filename self$files[1]. 2. Active bindings (active = list(...)) validate normalize parameter assignment (e.g. enum checks, .relPath() normalization, yesno() coercion). 3. $write() calls sequence insert*() helpers writeLines() result file.path(self$path, self$files[1]), self$add_file(...) registers auxiliary input files (climate, species, ecoregion, etc.) scenario can collect . adding new extension, mirror existing one closely — scenario assembler relies $type, $files[1], LandisData header set consistently.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Container scenario’s path, list LandisExtension objects, full set input files. scenario() R/scenarios.R top-level constructor: validates inputs, writes scenario .txt via insertSuccessionExtensions() / insertDisturbanceExtensions() / insertOtherExtensions() (partition extensions $type), registers climate/ecoregion/species/extension files returned LandisScenario. $replicate(n) method copies scenario directory <path>_rep01, <path>_rep02, … Monte Carlo runs.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Two complementary families free functions actual text generation data massaging: prep*() functions (e.g. prepInitialCommunities, prepSpeciesData, prepEcoregionParameters, prepFireReductionParameters, prepClimateConfig) take R-side data (often data.table/data.frame upstream LandR / Biomass_borealDataPrep workflows) convert LANDIS-II file formats disk, returning file paths data frames ready extensions. insert*() functions (mostly @keywords internal, R/ext_utils.R, R/utils.R, R/scenarios.R, ext_*.R) return character vectors LANDIS-II-formatted text lines extension’s $write() concatenates. Foundational primitives live R/utils.R: insertLandisData() (writes header + LandisData line), insertValue(), insertFile(), plus yesno() logical → "yes"/"" conversion .relPath() / .checkPath() path handling. generated files start landisutilsHeader() warning auto-generated.

text: Relative paths config files: paths written LANDIS-II input files must relative scenario/extension directory. Active bindings typically normalize incoming paths via .relPath(value, self$path) — preserve adding fields. data.table globals: new symbol used data.table non-standard evaluation needs listed utils::globalVariables() call R/landisutils-package.R (local call top file, R/ext_forc-succession.R) avoid R CMD check NOTEs. Collate order: DESCRIPTION explicit Collate: field several ext_*.R files use @include ext_utils.R. Running devtools::document() keeps sync — don’t hand-edit. Roxygen templates live man-roxygen/ referenced via @template param_path, @template return_file, etc. Spelling: spelling package used (see tests/spelling.R); add new domain terms inst/WORDLIST rather suppressing check. Extension test references: every ext_*.R extension must corresponding tests/testthat/test-ext_*.R file whose reference values come upstream LANDIS-II repo’s Core8 (v8) test input — .e. testings/Core8-* (testing/Core8-*) directory GitHub. Cite specific path URL ## NOTE: comment top test, prefer values copied verbatim input made-examples. PnET-Succession exception: testings/ directory upstream, test references deploy/examples/biomass-Pnet-succession-example-v8 instead. Raster pixel types LANDIS-II can read: LANDIS-II opens every map Landis.RasterIO.Gdal.GdalInputRaster.NewInputBand, accepts GDAL Byte, Int16, Int32, Float32 Float64 — terra terms INT1U, INT2S, INT4S, FLT4S, FLT8S. Anything else aborts run Raster band byte, short, int, float, double. rejected types exactly tempting ones: map codes, ecoregion codes fire-region codes positive construction, INT2U / INT4U look like natural fit cover range number bytes. INT1S — GDAL 3.7+ writes Int8, Byte. Never hand-pick datatype LANDIS-II map; call landis_datatype(max_value) (R/landis_datatype.R), returns smallest acceptable type. failure nasty diagnose: nothing rejects file write time, model dies seconds extension initialisation, R-side runner reports non-zero exit empty stderr — real message Landis-log.txt run directory. tests/testthat/test-landis_datatype.R carries static guard scans R/ datatype = "..." literals outside accepted set, bad type fails suite instead simulation. Config-syntax claims: PDF user guide extension’s src/ parser (e.g. *Parser.cs, MapFileNames.cs) Core8-* test inputs disagree placeholder/keyword/parameter name, trust parser + Core8 — PDFs sometimes stale (e.g. Extension-Output-Wildlife-Habitat v3 PDF documents {wildlife-name} parser Core8 input use {wildlifeName}). Succession-backend coupling: LANDIS-II scenario uses exactly one succession extension, disturbance/output extensions tied specific backend. Root Rot PnET Output (OutputBiomassPnET) consume PnET-specific cohort state (NSC, foliage stack, water balance) work PnET Succession — three always used together stack. Biomass Succession paired Root Rot PnET Output. disturbance/output extensions package succession-agnostic. package enforce ; check assembling scenarios, vignettes, integration tests. Naming: human-readable, suffix helpers (e.g. @family Climate BDA helpers, @family Land Use Plus helpers, @family Biomass Succession helpers). exact string must match across members family splits. Helpers genuinely shared extensions (e.g. suitabilityFile(), prepTopographyFile()) get one @family tag per consuming extension. use @seealso instead: free-form prose cross-extension references don’t belong single family — e.g. R6 class’s curated list shared scenario inputs ([prepClimateConfig()], [prepInitialCommunities()], [prepSpeciesData()]). @rdname caveat: functions share @rdname (e.g. prepGroundSlopeFile / prepUphillAzimuthMap aliased prepTopographyFile.Rd), put @family tag primary function — alias members otherwise duplicate family list inside shared Rd’s \seealso{} block. adding renaming helpers, run devtools::document() regenerate affected .Rd files.

title: Calibrating the Dynamic Fire System Extension
text: library project-agnostic expects provide: NFDB-style SpatVectors clipped primary fire regime (optionally secondary, broader regime context) – YEAR SIZE_HA columns points. fuel-type raster covering LANDIS simulation extent, mapping integer codes base fuel types (Conifer, ConiferPlantation, Deciduous, Slash, Open). Use bc_fuel_code_to_base() ’re working BC FUEL_TYPE_CD factor levels. production scenario directory ForCS / Dynamic Fuels / Dynamic Fire configs already written. calibration scenario template built copying patching. spun-IC: produced build_calibration_spinup_scenario() + run_calibration_spinup() – one LANDIS-II run pipeline build.

title: Calibrating the Dynamic Fire System Extension
text: functions designed composed inside project’s targets pipeline (workflow framework). typical wiring; numbered block one tar_target() calls practice.
code: ## 1. Observed fire targets (NFDB-derived; cheap; no LANDIS-II). save_observed_fire_targets(   primary_points   = nfdb_point_fru59,   primary_polys    = nfdb_poly_fru59,   secondary_points = nfdb_point_frt12, ## optional regional context   secondary_polys  = nfdb_poly_frt12,   fire_years       = 1950L:2023L,   fuel_types_rast  = fuel_types_rast,   path             = "outputs/calibration/observed_fire_targets.rds",   primary_label    = "FRU59",   secondary_label  = "FRT12"   ## fuel_code_to_base defaults to bc_fuel_code_to_base(); override if needed )  ## 2. Pre-calibration spinup: one LANDIS-II run with both ForCS spinup flags ON ##    to populate biomass; snapshot via the Output Biomass Community extension. ##    The snapshot's year-0 CSV+TIF become the calibration IC. build_calibration_spinup_scenario(   out_dir      = "LANDIS-II/_calibration_spinup",   template_dir = "LANDIS-II/phase_2_ICH",          ## any non-fire scenario will do   duration     = 1L,   cell_length  = 100L ) spinup_csv <- run_calibration_spinup(   scenario_dir = "LANDIS-II/_calibration_spinup",   base_seed    = 12345L,   method       = "docker" ) spinup_tif <- file.path(dirname(spinup_csv), "output-community-0.tif")  ## 3. Calibration scenario template: copy from a production fire scenario, swap ##    in the spinup IC, patch ForCS to skip succession, write a fresh baseline ##    dynamic-fire.txt from the supplied tables. build_calibration_scenario_template(   out_dir                    = "LANDIS-II/_calibration",   template_dir               = "LANDIS-II/phase_2_ICH_fire",   snapshot_ic_csv            = spinup_csv,   snapshot_ic_tif            = spinup_tif,   baseline_fire_size_table   = fire_size_table,   baseline_fuel_type_table   = defaultFuelTypeTable(),   baseline_fire_damage_table = defaultFireDamageTable(),   baseline_seasons_sim_table = seasons_sim_table,   sim_years                  = 10L,   cell_length                = 100L )  ## 4. DEoptim driver: starts a warm Docker pool, runs the calibration, tears ##    down on exit. Returns best_params (a named numeric of length 9) + the ##    DEoptim result object + a trace CSV. cfg <- list(   lower = c(     SeverityCalibrationFactor = 0.5,     SpHiProp = 0, SumHiProp = 0, FallHiProp = 0,     IgnProb_Conifer = 0, IgnProb_ConiferPlantation = 0,     IgnProb_Deciduous = 0, IgnProb_Slash = 0, IgnProb_Open = 0   ),   upper = c(     SeverityCalibrationFactor = 2.5,     SpHiProp = 1, SumHiProp = 1, FallHiProp = 1,     IgnProb_Conifer = 1.5, IgnProb_ConiferPlantation = 1.5,     IgnProb_Deciduous = 1.5, IgnProb_Slash = 1.5, IgnProb_Open = 1.5   ),   NP = 60L, itermax = 100L, n_reps = 5L, sim_years = 10L,   weights = c(count = 1, size = 1, area_fuel = 0, severity = 0),   simulator = "landis", method = "docker",   n_cores = max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 2L), parallel = TRUE,   base_seed = 12345L ) result <- calibrate_dynamic_fire(   observed_targets_path = "outputs/calibration/observed_fire_targets.rds",   scenario_template     = "LANDIS-II/_calibration/scenario.txt",   cfg                   = cfg,   out_dir               = "outputs/calibration" ) print(result$best_params)  ## 5. Apply calibrated params back to the production fire config (e.g., when ##    writing dynamic-fire.txt for the production scenarios). calibrated <- result$best_params production_fuel_type_table <- apply_calibrated_ignprob(   defaultFuelTypeTable(), calibrated ) production_fire_size_table <- apply_calibrated_hi_prop(   fire_size_table, calibrated ) production_severity_factor <- calibrated[["SeverityCalibrationFactor"]]

title: Calibrating the Dynamic Fire System Extension
text: library doesn’t ship target factory (deliberate – target naming conventions vary across consuming projects). Adopt helpers plain function calls inside tar_target(). Three things watch : Cycle avoidance. production tar_target writes dynamic-fire.txt consumes calibrated_fire_params (result calibrate_dynamic_fire()), calibration’s scenario template must transitively depend target. Use build_calibration_scenario_template()’s baseline_* arguments write fresh uncalibrated dynamic-fire.txt inline, depend per-extension file targets populate production scenario directory directly, scenario-assembly target. Deployment mode. calibration target run main process (deployment = "main" targets), crew worker, function internally manages FORK cluster n_cores workers + warm Docker pool n_cores containers. crew worker trying spawn cluster compete cores. DEoptim Suggest. Install via renv::install("DEoptim") running calibration target.

title: Calibrating the Dynamic Fire System Extension
text: sim_landis() per-trial cost dominated LANDIS-II Docker run (~1-3 minutes including dotnet startup). Total wall-clock production calibration: roughly NP * itermax * n_reps * per-trial / n_cores. warm Docker pool (started internally calibrate_dynamic_fire()) saves container-creation overhead dotnet startup, dominant cost remains LANDIS-II simulation . Practical levers calibration takes long: Cut sim_years 5 (instead 10): roughly half per-trial cost. Aggregate fuel_types_rast coarser resolution (e.g., 200 m cells) passing build_calibration_scenario_template(): ~4x speedup. Reduce NP × itermax; DEoptim’s evolutionary search compensates somewhat fewer evaluations. pure-R reimplementation (sim_r_reimpl(), currently stub) remove dotnet bottleneck entirely introduces maintenance burden tracking LANDIS-II’s evolving algorithm. See design notes _tmp_dynamic_fire_calibration.md gitanyow-partial-harvest project.

code: ext_lu <- LandUsePlus$new(   path = tmp_pth,   Timestep = 1L,   InputMaps = "landuse-{timestep}.tif",   SiteLog = "output/land-use/site-log.csv",   LandUses = list(     landUseType(       name = "forest",       mapCode = 4L,       allowHarvest = "no",       changes = landCoverChange(type = "NoChange")     ),     landUseType(       name = "FIPSandHarvest",       mapCode = 3L,       allowHarvest = "yes",       changes = list(         landCoverChange(           type = "RemoveTrees",           repeatHarvest = TRUE,           cohorts = list(             cohortSelector(               species = "acerrubr",               ranges = data.frame(low = 1, high = 200, percent = 20)             ),             cohortSelector(               species = "pinustro",               ranges = data.frame(low = 50, high = 300, percent = 30)             )           )         ),         landCoverChange(           type = "InsectDefoliation",           cohorts = cohortSelector(             species = "querrubr",             ranges = data.frame(low = 1, high = 300, percent = 60)           )         )       )     ),     landUseType(       name = "FIPS",       mapCode = 1L,       allowHarvest = "yes",       changes = landCoverChange(         type = "InsectDefoliation",         cohorts = list(           cohortSelector(             species = "querrubr",             ranges = data.frame(low = 1, high = 300, percent = 75)           ),           cohortSelector(             species = "pinustro",             ranges = data.frame(low = c(1, 71), high = c(62, 200), percent = c(20, 25))           )         )       )     )   ) ) ext_lu$write()

code: clim_years <- 2018:2019 ## availability is 1980 to last year  clim_data_path <- withr::local_tempdir("climate_data_")

title: Preparing Climate Data for Use With LANDIS-II
text: Daily weather fetched BioSIM using ClimaticEx_Daily model. high-level wrapper prep_daily_weather() takes study-area polygons object column name identifying ecoregions: Internally, prep_daily_weather() chains four lower-level helpers can call directly need finer control (e.g. schedule per-batch fetches dynamic targets):
code: climvars_daily <- c("prcp", "tmax", "tmin")  daily_weather <- prep_daily_weather(   vars = climvars_daily,   years = clim_years,   studyArea = ecoregionPolys,   id = "PolyID" )  head(daily_weather)  clim_file <- file.path(clim_data_path, "climate-data-daily.csv") writeClimateData(daily_weather, clim_file) ## 1. Build an elevation raster covering the study area (lon-lat). elev <- get_elevation_rast(ecoregionPolys, z = 9)  ## 2. Tile cells of `elev` that fall inside `ecoregionPolys` into batches. ##    Each row carries Longitude/Latitude/Elevation, plus EcoID (from the ##    studyArea field named by `id`) and BatchID (for parallel dispatch). locations_batch <- create_locations_df(   elev = elev,   studyArea = ecoregionPolys,   id = "PolyID",   batch_size = 500 )  ## 3. Fetch one (batch, year) at a time. Cap parallelism to <= 4 workers ##    so we don't overload the BioSIM web service. The cache is namespaced ##    by a short hash of `studyArea` so distinct study areas don't collide. future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 2)  sa_hash <- landisutils:::.studyArea_hash(ecoregionPolys)  grid <- expand.grid(batch = seq_along(locations_batch), year = clim_years) furrr::future_map2(grid$batch, grid$year, function(b, y) {   get_clim_daily(locations_batch[b], year = y, studyArea_hash = sa_hash, path = clim_data_path) })  ## 4. Read the partitioned Arrow CSV dataset, summarize by ecoregion, ##    and pivot to LANDIS-II Climate Library wide format. daily_weather <- assemble_climate_library_file(   dataset_path = file.path(clim_data_path, "ClimaticEx_Daily", sa_hash),   vars = c("Prcp", "Tmin", "Tmax"),   id_col = "EcoID" )

title: Preparing Climate Data for Use With LANDIS-II
text: CSV prep_daily_weather() / assemble_climate_library_file() produces consumed LANDIS-II Climate Library (Daily_RandomYears / Daily_AverageAllYears time series). Social Climate Fire extension reads daily fire-weather indirectly Climate Library computes FWI internally. assemble_climate_library_file_scf() thin wrapper emits table lowercase Variable spellings used Social-Climate-Fire reference input (LTB_ClimateInputs_91_10_v2.csv): precip, maxtemp, mintemp, windspeed, winddirection. Climate Library parser case-insensitive, either spelling works input — pick whichever scenario template expects.
code: ## populate the BioSIM cache with the 5 SCF variables prep_daily_weather(   vars = c("prcp", "tmax", "tmin", "ws", "wnddir"),   years = clim_years,   studyArea = ecoregionPolys,   id = "PolyID" )  sa_hash <- landisutils:::.studyArea_hash(ecoregionPolys) scenario_tag <- landisutils:::.biosim_scenario_tag("RCP45", "RCM4")  scf_inputs <- assemble_climate_library_file_scf(   dataset_path = file.path(clim_data_path, "ClimaticEx_Daily", sa_hash, scenario_tag),   vars = c("Prcp", "Tmin", "Tmax", "WndS", "WndD"),   id_col = "EcoID" )  clim_file <- file.path(clim_data_path, "scf-climate-inputs.csv") writeClimateData(scf_inputs, clim_file)

title: Preparing Climate Data for Use With LANDIS-II
text: want monthly weather co-located daily BioSIM cells (elevation raster, point batches), use prep_monthly_weather_biosim() — shares elevation/batching machinery prep_daily_weather() fetches BioSIM’s Climatic_Monthly model. Wind variables (ws, wnddir) pulled call BioSIM’s companion ClimaticWind_Monthly model; wind -direction summarised across model’s 36 directional bins (W0..W350) using frequency-weighted circular mean: lower-level helpers (get_clim_monthly(), assemble_climate_library_file_monthly()) mirror daily pipeline need schedule per-batch fetches dynamic targets:
code: climvars_monthly_biosim <- c("prcp", "tmax", "tmin", "temp", "rh", "srad", "ws", "wnddir")  monthly_weather_biosim <- prep_monthly_weather_biosim(   vars = climvars_monthly_biosim,   years = clim_years,   studyArea = ecoregionPolys,   id = "PolyID" )  head(monthly_weather_biosim)  clim_file <- file.path(clim_data_path, "climate-data-monthly-biosim.csv") writeClimateData(monthly_weather_biosim, clim_file) elev <- get_elevation_rast(ecoregionPolys, z = 9) locations_batch <- create_locations_df(   elev = elev,   studyArea = ecoregionPolys,   id = "PolyID",   batch_size = 500 )  future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 2)  sa_hash <- landisutils:::.studyArea_hash(ecoregionPolys)  grid <- expand.grid(batch = seq_along(locations_batch), year = clim_years) furrr::future_map2(grid$batch, grid$year, function(b, y) {   get_clim_monthly(locations_batch[b], year = y, studyArea_hash = sa_hash, path = clim_data_path) })  monthly_weather_biosim <- assemble_climate_library_file_monthly(   dataset_path = file.path(clim_data_path, "Climatic_Monthly", sa_hash),   vars = c("TotalPrcp", "MeanTmin", "MeanTmax", "WndS", "WndD"),   id_col = "EcoID" )

title: Preparing Climate Data for Use With LANDIS-II
text: climr provides ClimateNA-style change-factor downscaling PRISM/DAYMET composite reference grid North America. Historical observational years span 1901-2024 (obs_ts_dataset = "climatena" "cru.gpcc"). lower-level helpers (get_clim_monthly_climr(), assemble_climate_library_file_monthly_climr()) mirror BioSIM pipeline need schedule per-year fetches dynamic targets. climr’s -disk cache configured via options("climr.cache.path" = ...); prep_monthly_weather_climr() defaults climr/ subdirectory getOption("landisutils.cache.path") duration call.
code: climvars_monthly_climr <- c("prcp", "tmax", "tmin", "temp", "rh", "cmd")  monthly_weather_climr <- prep_monthly_weather_climr(   vars = climvars_monthly_climr,   years = clim_years,   studyArea = ecoregionPolys,   id = "PolyID" )  head(monthly_weather_climr)  clim_file <- file.path(clim_data_path, "climate-data-monthly-climr.csv") writeClimateData(monthly_weather_climr, clim_file)

title: Preparing Climate Data for Use With LANDIS-II
text: prep_*() functions used historical/observational weather can also produce future weather climate-change scenarios. Two complementary sources wired : BioSIM (CMIP5-era): prep_daily_weather() prep_monthly_weather_biosim() accept rcp clim_model arguments forwarded BioSIM::generateWeather(). rcp one "CONSTANT_CLIMATE", "RCP45", "RCP85"; clim_model one "RCM4" (Canadian Regional Climate Model 4, CanESM2-driven), "GCM4" (CGCM4 / CanESM2-family GCM), "Hadley" (HadGEM). climr (CMIP6): prep_monthly_weather_climr() accepts gcms, ssps, max_run arguments forwarded climr::downscale(). Pass subset climr::list_gcms() (use bcgov-recommended 8-member subset exposed climr_ensemble_8) subset climr::list_ssps(). BioSIM climr caches namespaced scenario, historical future fetches study area coexist disk without colliding.

title: Preparing Climate Data for Use With LANDIS-II
text: Pass rcp clim_model straight prep_daily_weather(). Canadian fourth-generation GCM (CGCM4 / CanESM2-family) corresponds BioSIM’s clim_model = "GCM4": arguments also accepted prep_monthly_weather_biosim(), lets pull wind (ws, wnddir) shortwave-radiation (srad) variables matching scenario - climr expose either, pair BioSIM need wind radiation future projection.
code: climvars_daily <- c("prcp", "tmax", "tmin")  daily_weather_future <- prep_daily_weather(   vars = climvars_daily,   years = clim_years_future,   studyArea = ecoregionPolys,   id = "PolyID",   rcp = "RCP45",   clim_model = "GCM4" )  head(daily_weather_future)  clim_file <- file.path(clim_data_path, "climate-data-daily-rcp45-canesm.csv") writeClimateData(daily_weather_future, clim_file)

title: Preparing Climate Data for Use With LANDIS-II
text: prep_monthly_weather_climr() switches projection mode whenever gcms non-NULL. bcgov-recommended 8-member subset climr::list_gcms() exposed convenience climr_ensemble_8; see https://bcgov.github.io/climr/articles/guidance_ensembleSelection.html rationale. SSP2-4.5 ("ssp245") standard CMIP6 analogue CMIP5 RCP 4.5: row multi-GCM ensemble mean across 8 members, taken inside assemble_climate_library_file_monthly_climr(), output (Year, Month, Variable, <ecoregion-id>...) shape observational pipeline. Set max_run > 0 additionally average multiple runs per GCM (climr defaults ensemble-mean , max_run = 0).
code: climvars_monthly_climr <- c("prcp", "tmax", "tmin", "temp", "rh", "cmd")  monthly_weather_climr_future <- prep_monthly_weather_climr(   vars = climvars_monthly_climr,   years = clim_years_future,   studyArea = ecoregionPolys,   id = "PolyID",   gcms = climr_ensemble_8,   ssps = "ssp245",   max_run = 0L )  head(monthly_weather_climr_future)  clim_file <- file.path(clim_data_path, "climate-data-monthly-climr-ssp245-ens8.csv") writeClimateData(monthly_weather_climr_future, clim_file)

Required keys (numeric): RMin, RMax, MortalityMin, MortalityMax, PredationMin, PredationMax, HarvestMin, HarvestMax. ConsumptionRate Integer (kg/yr/individual; §4.2.7). ANPPForageProp Numeric [0, 1]; proportion ANPP counts forage (§4.2.8; default 0.66). MinBrowsePropinReach Numeric [0, 1]; minimum proportion browse within reach cohort browsed (§4.2.9). BrowseBiomassThreshold Numeric [0, 1]; proportion ecoregion max biomass cohorts begin escape browse (§4.2.12). BrowseBiomassThresholdMin, BrowseBiomassThresholdMax (Optional) Numeric [0, 1]; thresholds ForageInReachMethod = "LinearEachCohort" form (§4.2.10–4.2.11). CountNonForageinSitePref Logical; optional, default FALSE (§4.2.17). UseInitBiomassAsForage Logical; optional, default FALSE (§4.2.18). ForageInReachMethod Character; one "Ordered" "LinearEachCohort"; optional, default "Ordered" (§4.2.19). Simulated area--fuel comes event's ignition fuel code times DamagedSites, mapped base fuel types via observed$fuel_code_to_base. Skipped (contributes 0) either observed$primary$area_by_fuel_ha NULL observed$fuel_code_to_base missing. L_severity: chi-squared distance simulated observed severity-class proportions. Simulated severities come event's MeanSeverity binned integer classes 1..5; observed comes observed$primary$severity_dist (5-element named numeric vector summing 1). Skipped observed NULL. component values unitless non-negative; chi-squared components use small epsilon denominator avoid division zero empty observed bins.

title: Prepare Climate Data — prep_daily_weather
text: vars character specifying climate variables (lowercase, e.g. "prcp", "tmax", "tmin"). years integer vector specifying years. studyArea sf polygons object delineating e.g., ecoregions fire zones. id character specifying name column/field studyArea identifying ecoregions. batch_size integer maximum cells per BioSIM batch call. Default 1000. Smaller values yield parallel-friendly chunks. z integer zoom level passed elevatr::get_elev_raster() underlying elevation raster. Higher values give finer raster (point cells fed BioSIM/climr); lower values give coarser raster (fewer cells, fewer batches, faster fetches). Default 9 (~250 m mid-latitudes). tests / smoke runs, values around 5-7 typically yield single BioSIM batch small study area. rcp character. BioSIM representative concentration pathway. One "CONSTANT_CLIMATE", "RCP45", "RCP85". Default "RCP45". used BioSIM pipelines (prep_daily_weather(), prep_monthly_weather_biosim()). See Climate projections (BioSIM, CMIP5). clim_model character. BioSIM climate model. One "RCM4", "GCM4", "Hadley". Default "RCM4". used BioSIM pipelines. ref_grid optional fixed reference SpatRaster GLOBAL per-cell cache. cell numbers taken STABLE GLOBAL ids cell VALUES read BioSIM elevation (elevM) – MUST carry elevation values (e.g. DEM resampled onto grid). supplied, monthly pull cached global ids one shared, accumulating store, overlapping / nested study areas reuse cells already fetched. NULL (default), per-study-area elevatr grid (z) used. obs_ts_dataset character. climr observational time-series dataset. One "climatena" "cru.gpcc". Default "climatena". used prep_monthly_weather_climr() observational mode. gcms character vector CMIP6 GCM names (subset climr::list_gcms()). NULL (default), prep_monthly_weather_climr() runs observational mode; set, projection mode. bcgov-recommended eight-member ensemble exposed climr_ensemble_8. used prep_monthly_weather_climr(). ssps character vector CMIP6 SSP names (subset climr::list_ssps(), e.g. "ssp245"). Required gcms set. used prep_monthly_weather_climr(). max_run integer number ensemble runs per GCM fetch climr (averaged together ensemble_mean = TRUE, climr default). Default 0L (climr's default; uses ensemble mean ). used prep_monthly_weather_climr().

title: Prepare Climate Data — prep_daily_weather
text: tbl_df columns Year, Month, Variable, one column per ecoregion (named id values). Daily output (prep_daily_weather()) additionally carries Day column.

title: Prepare Climate Data — prep_daily_weather

text: save_observed_fire_targets() gains min_size_ha argument (default 1.0) truncates fire_sizes_ha lower bound persists value output payload. Set min_size_ha = 0 restore prior behaviour. loss_from_stats() reads observed$min_size_ha applies lower truncation pooled sim_sizes KS statistic compares like--like. loss_from_stats() now subsamples sim_sizes length(obs_sizes) (deterministic seed; override via getOption("landisutils.calibration.subsample_seed", 12345L)) KS test whenever length(sim_sizes) >= 2 * length(obs_sizes). Removes “samples -> better-resolved tail -> bigger KS gap” artifact driving DEoptim toward body-matching expense tail fidelity. loss_from_stats() adds new loss component, size_tail = |log10(sim_q95) - log10(obs_q95)| (default weight 1), explicitly checking upper-tail magnitude. KS distance routinely -weights tail log-scaled data; size_tail gives DEoptim separate gradient close q95 gap. Components vector now c(count, size, size_tail, area_fuel, severity) (new entry; downstream code introspects components names needs updating). .chi_sq_severity() switched pmax(obs_p, 1e-6) Laplace-smoothed denominators (alpha = 0.01 per bin default; override via getOption("landisutils.calibration.severity_smoothing_alpha", 0.01)). previous regulariser gave empty observed severity class ~1e6 multiplier chi-sq contribution, even 1% simulated mass empty observed bin dominated every component loss; smoothing caps worst-case contribution meaningful magnitude without otherwise distorting comparison.

title: landisutils 0.0.24
text: loss_from_stats() now computes L_area_fuel L_severity corresponding observed components present payload; previously stubbed zero. title: landisutils 0.0.24
text: new function family calibrating LANDIS-II Dynamic Fire System extension. calibration tunes SeverityCalibrationFactor, per-season FMC HiProp values, per-base-fuel-type IgnProb multipliers simulated fires match observed regional fire statistics; empirically-fit parameters (Mu, Sigma, Max, NumFires, seasonal PropFire) fit data layer upstream part optimisation. Observed-target builder (one-time NFDB-derived summaries): save_observed_fire_targets() – writes small .rds per-ecoregion observed summaries. Project-agnostic: primary / secondary ecoregion SpatVectors + fuel_code_to_base mapping caller-provided. bc_fuel_code_to_base() – default fuel-code mapping BC FUEL_TYPE_CD factor encoding (codes 1..13); pass custom mapping project’s fuel-classification raster uses different encoding. Scenario builders static-landscape calibration scenario: build_calibration_spinup_scenario() – builds one-LANDIS-II scenario runs ForCS spinup flags emits snapshot spun-cohort community via Output Biomass Community extension. year-0 snapshot becomes calibration IC. run_calibration_spinup() – blocking single-trial LANDIS-II invocation spinup; dispatches landis_run_local() / landis_run_docker(). build_calibration_scenario_template() – copies production fire scenario, swaps IC spinup snapshot, patches ForCS calibration (spinup + frozen succession), optionally writes fresh baseline dynamic-fire.txt inline (breaks cycle calibrated_fire_params-aware production fire config calibration loop). write_landis_scenario_file() (scenarios.R) – lower-level scenario.txt writer takes already-written extension config-file paths rather R6 extension objects. Useful project pipelines write extension configs separate steps. Warm Docker pool calibration: landis_pool_start() / landis_pool_exec() / landis_pool_stop() – pool detached LANDIS-II containers docker execs per DEoptim trial instead docker run --rm per trial. Per-call env overrides (HOME=/tmp, DOTNET_BUNDLE_EXTRACT_BASE_DIR=...) keep dotnet accreting per-user-cache state trials. Designed .exit() teardown calibration drivers. Simulator backends calibration loop: sim_landis() – per-trial LANDIS-II invocation. Takes file paths (FORK-safe), copies template -> scratch dir, patches dynamic-fire.txt, runs LANDIS-II either via warm pool one-landis_run_docker() / landis_run_local(), parses logs. sim_r_reimpl() – reserved slot future pure-R reimplementation; currently errors -yet-implemented message. sim_mock() – plausibly-shaped output testing calibration driver’s control flow without Docker. DEoptim driver: calibrate_dynamic_fire() – orchestrates calibration: starts warm Docker pool, sets FORK cluster per-worker container pinning, invokes DEoptim::DEoptim() multi-component loss objective, tears pool + cluster via .exit(). Gated requireNamespace("DEoptim") (DEoptim Suggests; install via renv::install("DEoptim") calling). Vignette: vignette("Dynamic-Fire-Calibration", package = "landisutils") documents end--end target-wiring pattern downstream projects. Tests: 97+ testthat expectations across calibration + pool test files. Docker-gated tests skip_if_not() docker unavailable; DEoptim-gated driver tests skip_if_not_installed("DEoptim").

title: landisutils 0.0.23
text: cpu_limit = 4: maps docker run --cpus. LANDIS-II compute single-threaded (~1 core), .NET runtime spins 9-11 OS threads GC thread pool, 4 comfortable default. Pass NULL limit. mem_limit = "8g": baseline RAM cap (maps docker run --memory). Accepts numeric byte count string like "4g" / "512m". Pass NULL (mem_limit = Inf) limit. mem_margin = 1.5: headroom factor applied previously-observed peak (see auto-resolution ). Auto-resolution prior resource logs. running, function reads existing <rep_dir>/log/{docker,local}_resources.log rep. peak_mem_bytes * mem_margin exceeds baseline mem_limit, limit raised value rep ran fine last time never killed cap rerun. prior log exists rep (first run, rep dir freshly deleted), memory cap dropped entirely first run can discover needs; subsequent runs inherit empirically observed peak. CPU limit constant regardless history: LANDIS-II single-threaded .NET runtime doesn’t scale available cores.

title: landisutils 0.0.22
text: landis_run_docker() landis_run_local() now append three additional lines rep’s docker_resources.log / local_resources.log: makes per-rep resource log self-describing: downstream provenance tooling can recover just rep used (elapsed_sec, peak_mem_bytes) host ran , important reps dispatched across heterogeneous cluster. New exported helpers: host_cpu_info() returns list(model, n_logical, ram_bytes), cross-platform: /proc/cpuinfo + /proc/meminfo Linux, sysctl machdep.cpu.brand_string + hw.memsize macOS, PROCESSOR_IDENTIFIER env var + wmic ComputerSystem ... TotalPhysicalMemory Windows. Logical-core count uses parallel::detectCores() everywhere. Called automatically run helpers. read_landis_resource_logs(run_dir) parses *_resources.log run_dir returns one data.frame row per rep fields. Used downstream report tooling summarise run-time / memory / host across replicates.
code: host_cpu_model: <model name>          # e.g. "AMD EPYC 7702 64-Core Processor" host_cpu_cores: <N>                   # logical cores visible to R host_ram_bytes: <N>                   # total system memory in bytes

title: landisutils 0.0.21
text: prepTopographyFile() (prepGroundSlopeFile() / prepUphillAzimuthMap() wrappers) now replaces NoData cells 0 writing INT2S raster. terra::terrain() leaves edge cells NaN (full 3x3 neighbourhood), becomes -32768 sentinel INT2S. LANDIS-II’s Dynamic Fire reader rejects active cell value: bug latent grids active cells, exposed whenever upstream changes (e.g. corrected non-veg masks) expand active area 1-cell edge band terrain raster. flat default (0 deg) safe: single-cell edge contributes negligibly Dynamic Fire’s rate--spread.

title: landisutils 0.0.20
text: skip check tar_landis() now input-aware. Previously run skipped whenever <rep_dir>/Landis-log.txt existed contained “Model run complete”, regardless whether inputs changed. meant targets correctly re-evaluated run target upstream input change (e.g. regenerated initial-communities.tif ecoregions.tif), surrounding command ran skip check still fired, landis_run_docker() / landis_run_local() never invoked rep dir kept stale outputs previous run. fix writes <rep_dir>/log/input_hash.json sidecar successful run, capturing SHA-1 (per-input-file MD5 + base_seed + rep_index + scenario_file). skip check now also requires saved hash match current input hash; mismatch triggers real rerun. New force = FALSE argument tar_landis(). Setting force = TRUE short-circuits skip check LANDIS-II always runs (useful debugging one-forced reruns without deleting rep dirs). Migration: existing rep dirs lack log/input_hash.json, first tar_make() upgrading rebuilds every rep. safe-conservative behaviour: can’t know whether existing outputs correspond current inputs. Users know rep current can sidestep rerun writing hash file manually.

title: landisutils 0.0.19
text: landis_run_docker() now writes <scenario_dir>/log/docker_image.log containing immutable sha256 digest image used run (<repo>@sha256:<64hex>, falling back local Id images registry origin). Image tags mutable; digest canonical identifier bytes actually ran. Downstream provenance tooling can read sidecar pin run specific image regardless subsequent tag movement. New pull = FALSE argument; TRUE, docker pull <image> runs simulation captured digest reflects current registry rather possibly-stale local copy. argument also exposed via tar_landis(pull = ...).

title: landisutils 0.0.18
text: leading_species() now returns "Non-vegetated" cells total biomass across species zero, instead falling alphabetical tiebreaker (arbitrarily assigned "Ac" defoliated cells). matches existing community_label() behaviour means transition / alluvial plots accurately reflect fire harvest impacts.

title: landisutils 0.0.17
text: Breaking API change: tar_landis() longer accepts n_reps. now takes explicit rep_index argument (unquoted upstream target symbol) returns single tar_target object (original API). caller creates rep-index target explicitly inside module list() alongside tar_landis() call. keeps targets visible tarborist’s static AST analysis (tarborist.additionalSingleTargetFactories handles run target; literal tar_target() call handles rep-index target): iteration = "vector" rep-index target enables cross() iterate individual elements, giving n_scenarios x n_reps independent branches dispatched crew workers parallel. branch runs one LANDIS-II simulation tracks replicate’s output files. Previously n_reps simulations ran inside single loop within one target branch. Caching scaling: adding replicates creates new branches – existing replicate results remain cached. Changing one replicate’s inputs invalidates branch. Previously change invalidated replicates.
code: list(   tar_target(name = ..._rep_index, command = seq_len(5L), iteration = "vector"),   landisutils::tar_landis(name = ..., rep_index = ..._rep_index, ...,                           pattern = cross(scenario_dir, ..._rep_index)) )

title: landisutils 0.0.17
text: landis_replicate() gains rep_index parameter single-replicate creation. Pass rep_index = (instead n_reps = N) create exactly one replicate directory (repNN/) without touching others. Useful replicate dispatched crew worker. n_reps now keyword-; positional second-argument form still works n_reps = clearer. function now requires exactly one n_reps rep_index. seed assigned rep_index used (base_seed + rep_index - 1) matches seed assigned n_reps mode index, results reproducible regardless call form used.

what: Vegetation dynamics: species biomass and transition plots
title: landisutils 0.0.16
text: New read_biomass_c_snapshots(paths, times, run_name) reads ForCS log_BiomassC.csv files (per-cohort, per-cell) one replicates, filtering requested snapshot years via arrow::open_dataset() lazy streaming multi-GB files never need fully materialised R. ForCS writes log_BiomassC.csv unconditionally, additional output extension required. New read_biomass_output_rasters(dirs, times, species, live_map_pattern, run_name) succession-agnostic alternative: reads per-species biomass rasters written Output.Biomass v4 extension (present landis-ii-v8-release Docker image). Works succession extension; requires Output.Biomass included scenario configuration. readers return identical data.table schema (scenario, replicate, Time, row, column, [ecoregion,] species, biomass Mg C ha^-1), downstream functions source-agnostic. New biomass_landscape_summary(df) aggregates per-cell snapshot data landscape-mean ± SD biomass species per timestep. New leading_species(df) labels cell snapshot species highest total live biomass. Ties broken alphabetically. New community_label(df, n_spp, min_pct) labels cell top-n species combination (e.g. "Hw-Sx"); species min_pct cell total dropped; zero-biomass cells labelled "Non-vegetated". New transition_data(label_df, times) builds lodes-form tibble required ggalluvial: unique label-path combinations across snapshot years, cell counts averaged across replicates. New plot_species_biomass(summary_df, colours, title) produces stacked area chart landscape-mean biomass species time. New plot_transitions(lodes_df, colours, title) produces Sankey-style alluvial diagram (via ggalluvial) showing cells move vegetation types across snapshot years. arrow, ggalluvial, ggplot2, purrr added Imports (previously absent Suggests).

title: landisutils 0.0.15
text: landis_run_docker(): container names now include calling process PID random integer suffix prevent name collisions multiple LANDIS replicates run simultaneously. tar_landis(): dependency file lists now deduplicated passed landis_replicate(). Paths normalised absolute form, filtered existing files, deduplicated basename; scenario-specific files (scenario directory) take priority cross-scenario duplicates. Applies Docker local run paths. tar_landis(): replicates LANDIS-II already completed successfully now skipped (idempotent re-run). Completion detected presence “Model run complete” Landis-log.txt. Applies Docker local run paths.

title: landisutils 0.0.14
text: insertDOMPools() now wraps multi-word pool names double-quotes, matching LANDIS-II parser’s requirement (e.g. "Fast AG" instead Fast AG). ForCS v4 changed four large parameter tables inline text CSV file references. insertEcoSppDOMParameters(), insertANPPTimeSeries(), insertMaxBiomassTimeSeries(), insertEstablishProbabilities() now write CSV path emit Keyword "filename" reference line, matching ForCS v4.0.2 input format. ForCS$write() passes self$path four CSV-writing insert*() functions registers resulting files via add_file() landis_replicate() copies replicate directory. four ForCS CSV filenames now prefixed ForCS_ (ForCS_EcoSppDOMParameters.csv, ForCS_ANPPTimeSeries.csv, ForCS_MaxBiomassTimeSeries.csv, ForCS_EstablishProbabilities.csv) origin unambiguous alongside extension files.

title: landisutils 0.0.14
text: LandisExtension subclasses produce fixed-name output files now expose output_files active binding listing files relative paths (e.g. log CSVs, summary CSVs). Extensions fixed outputs inherit base LandisExtension$output_files returns character(0). LandisScenario gains output_files active binding returns two LANDIS-II core outputs always written scenario directory: Landis-log.txt Metadata/LANDIS-II v8.0/LANDIS-II v8.0.xml. scenario() now writes output_manifest.txt scenario directory, listing fixed-name output files declared scenario extensions. manifest registered scenario$files landis_replicate() copies replicate directory. tar_landis() now reads output_manifest.txt base scenario directory includes listed files (absolute paths per replicate) returned character vector alongside log/ scan output_dir scan. ensures targets tracks log CSVs, Landis-log.txt, Metadata XML explicitly, without relying glob discovery.

title: landisutils 0.0.14
text: landis_run_docker() now tracks wall-clock elapsed time peak container memory. Docker launched via callr::r_bg() main thread can poll docker stats ---stream every 2 s; maximum observed RSS recorded peak memory. named container (e.g. landis-run-20260527123456) used stats lookup removed automatically --rm. Results printed completion written <scenario_dir>/log/docker_resources.log. --user uid:gid flag now skipped Windows (id -u/id -g available ; Docker Desktop Windows require ). landis_run_local() now tracks wall-clock elapsed time peak process memory. system2() replaced processx::process$new() (exposes subprocess PID handles working directory directly), main thread polls ps::ps_memory_info() every 2 s. ps package cross-platform, memory tracking works Linux, macOS, Windows without platform-specific shell commands. Results printed completion written <scenario_dir>/log/local_resources.log. functions now return named list (exit_code, elapsed_sec, peak_mem_bytes) instead bare integer exit code. processx ps added Imports (previously available transitive dependencies callr).

title: landisutils 0.0.13
text: DynamicFire$write() now calls add_file() InitialWeatherDatabase copied replicate directories landis_replicate(). Previously weather CSV silently absent, causing LANDIS-II fail runtime. tar_landis() output_dir now accepts character vector output subdirectory names. Pass c("output", "fire") using Dynamic Fire extension, writes maps event/summary logs fire/ subdirectory inside scenario directory.

title: landisutils 0.0.12
text: insertFile(), insertLandisData(), insertValue() now exported project-level code can build custom scenario files using primitives package uses internally. landis_find_docker() new helper returns path Landis.Console.dll inside container, reading getOption("landisutils.docker.console"). landis_run_docker() now calls instead duplicating lookup. landis_replicate() gains base_seed argument. set, RandomNumberSeed replicate’s scenario.txt rewritten base_seed + (rep_index - 1), giving every replicate distinct deterministic seed. Seeds index-stable: adding replicates later never changes seeds existing ones. tar_landis() gains base_seed argument, passed landis_replicate() baked command expression factory-call time crew workers receive correct value.

title: landisutils 0.0.11
text: Pin santoku GitHub source (hughjonesd/santoku) package archived CRAN 2026-05-15, broke zonal dependency resolution GitHub Actions CI.

text: Remove unused PredictiveEcology packages: LandR, SpaDES.core, SpaDES.tools, reproducible, scfmutils, map – due broken dependency resolution.

title: landisutils 0.0.9
text: landis_run(): fix inverted stopifnot() guard — function previously rejected valid LandisScenario objects accepted everything else. New landis_run_docker() runs LANDIS-II simulation ephemeral Docker container (bind-mounting scenario directory /sim). New landis_run_local() runs LANDIS-II simulation directly via dotnet, writing stdout/stderr <scenario_dir>/log/. New tar_landis() factory creates targets format = "file" target runs LANDIS-II (locally via Docker) returns tracked output log files. New package options landisutils.docker.image landisutils.run.method set .onLoad().

title: landisutils 0.0.7
text: prep_monthly_weather_climr() longer silently advertises "srad" supported variable. Vignette examples updated. get_elevation_rast() gained tmp_dir argument (default <landisutils.cache.path>/elevatr_tiles/) AWS Terrain Tile downloads land package cache instead leaking R session’s global tempdir() (elevatr’s default). climate test cleanup: new local_climate_test_cache() test helper (tests/testthat/helper-climate-cleanup.R) routes cache option, child-process TMPDIR, JVM java.io.tmpdir (used J4R J4RServer*.log hsperfdata_<user>/) per-test withr::local_tempdir(), tears future::plan(multisession) exit, BioSIM/climr/elevatr fetch tests longer accumulate /tmp residue across runs.
